CLIENT NOTICE

Submission of an intake request does not automatically establish attorney-client representation until accepted by the firm. Availability and response times may vary based on staffing, urgency, conflicts, and case complexity.

Rules & Policies

01 / POLICY

Can my case be denied?

Yes. The firm may decline due to conflicts of interest, insufficient evidence, frivolous claims, policy violations, or attorney availability.

Intake system misuse

Misuse of emergency or intake systems may result in denial of services, administrative action, Firm Blacklist, or ticket closure.

Truthfulness

False information can severely impact a case and may result in termination of representation.

Availability

Attorneys are not available 24/7. Emergency requests are monitored when possible and depend on staffing and activity.

Communication & Representation

02 / CONTACT

Response times

General inquiries: 12–24 hours
Criminal matters: As available
High-priority criminal: Immediate attention when possible

Requesting an attorney

You may request a specific attorney, but assignment depends on availability, conflicts, and case specialization.

If your attorney is unavailable

Another firm representative may assist temporarily depending on urgency.

Multiple attorneys

Larger or more serious cases may involve multiple legal staff.

Billing & Fees

03 / BILLING

What determines cost?

Costs depend on case complexity, attorney time, emergency response needs, court appearances, and investigation work.

Retainers & deposits

Some matters may require retainers or deposits before representation begins.

Initial consultations

Initial consultation arrangements may vary depending on the matter and attorney availability.

Refunds

Refunds are handled case-by-case and are not guaranteed once substantial legal work has begun.

FOIA Requests

04 / RECORDS

FOIA allows citizens to request access to certain public government records.

Information that may be covered

  • Marriage and divorce records
  • Arrests, incidents, and law-enforcement reports
  • Footage from government-owned properties
  • Past expungements
  • Commercial property registration information
  • Additional records held by a government agency

Common exemptions

  • Classified national-security information
  • Information barred from release by law
  • Trade secrets or confidential commercial data
  • Privileged communications
  • Personal privacy information
  • Certain law-enforcement records
  • Phone numbers and privately owned real estate
  • LEO disposition or punishments

What a FOIA request needs

  • Information sought
  • Department providing it
  • Relevant officer names or call signs, if applicable
  • Date ranges and event times

Submit via: Appointments → FOIA Inquiry

FOIA timing

Confirmation or clarification should be received within 5 days. Most FOIAs should take no longer than 5 days; complex requests may take up to 10 days.

Timelines may change due to external agency communications or availability.

Expungement

05 / RECORDS

Eligibility

Eligibility is determined by offense type, time since conviction or arrest, criminal history, and judicial approval. Not all offenses qualify.

Potentially expungable

  • Certain dismissed charges
  • Minor offenses
  • Older convictions
  • Non-violent charges

What expungement means

Expungement does not always completely erase records. Some records may remain accessible to courts or law enforcement depending on applicable rules.

Timing

Timing can depend on court backlog, record complexity, and judicial review timelines.

Civil Litigation

06 / CIVIL

Can a civil case settle?

Yes. Civil cases can settle through negotiation, settlement agreements, or mediation, which may reduce court time and legal expenses.

How long does it take?

Timing depends on court scheduling, complexity, evidence availability, and settlement negotiations.

Useful evidence

  • Contracts
  • Screenshots
  • Financial records
  • Messages
  • Video clips
  • Witness testimony
  • Business agreements

Types of civil matters

  • Contract disputes
  • Property disputes
  • Financial disagreements
  • Business conflicts
  • Negligence claims
  • Breach of agreement cases
  • Certain lawsuits against individuals or organizations

Criminal Defense

07 / DEFENSE
Possible outcomes
Charges may potentially be reduced or dismissed. Outcomes depend on evidence, officer conduct, legal procedure compliance, witness credibility, prosecutorial decisions, and judicial rulings. No outcome is guaranteed.
Evidence attorneys may review
Bodycam footage, dashcam footage, screenshots, witness statements, arrest reports, video recordings, audio recordings, and MDT records. These can be acquired by attorneys through FOIA.
Investigative questions
The firm generally recommends waiting for legal counsel before answering investigative questions.
Active police scenes & investigations
Attorneys may respond during active police scenes depending on availability; may attend interrogations, negotiate with law enforcement, and provide legal advice during investigations. Availability is not guaranteed during every emergency.
What happens after criminal intake?
Intake staff reviews the request; an attorney may contact you for more information; evidence and reports are reviewed; representation terms are discussed; and the attorney prepares a legal defense strategy.

Criminal matters

  • Arrests
  • Warrants
  • Felony charges
  • Misdemeanors
  • Drug charges
  • Weapons charges
  • Investigations
  • Traffic-related criminal offenses
  • Violations of state law

If arrested

  • Remain calm
  • Do not resist arrest
  • Request an attorney immediately
  • Avoid unnecessary statements to law enforcement
  • Open a Criminal Intake ticket as soon as possible
